traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 24 Rosaceae, 68 Ulmaceae, 71 Urticaceae, 200 Elaeagnaceae and 201 Rhamnaceae, with the figs and mulberries, which make APG's Rosales: leaves mostly with stipules, paired and often soon falling; Elaeagnaceae have none.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): Rosaceae leaves usually spiral, rarely opposite. Opposite 'sometimes' for Urticaceae (Pilea, Urtica), some Rhamnaceae, Barbeya, and Cannabis/Humulus (my knowledge).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): Rosaceae usually spiral, never clearly two-ranked. Two-ranked leaves in the elm/hackberry/fig group and opposite pairs in many nettles are my knowledge; weighting by Rosaceae and Moraceae (Ficus spiral).

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): Rosaceae often compound (Rosoideae), otherwise the order's families have simple blades; Cannabaceae palmately lobed or compound (Wikipedia Cannabaceae).

traits.division_pattern.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): Rosaceae often compound (roses, rowans, agrimonies pinnate; brambles, cinquefoils, strawberries palmate/ternate). 'usually pinnate' is my weighting.

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): order mostly trees, shrubs and leafy herbs; basal rosettes only in some Rosoideae herbs (Fragaria, Potentilla, Alchemilla). Inferred weighting.

traits.life_span.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): trees, shrubs, perennial herbs; annuals few (some nettles, Cannabis per Wikipedia Cannabaceae).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): reduced wind-pollinated flowers in the urticalean group, open radial flowers in Rosaceae; Wikipedia Cannabaceae: actinomorphic.

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb, Rosales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): hypanthium present; the urticalean families lack it (Moraceae, Urticaceae state false already).

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): Rosaceae carpels free and superior in many, at least half inferior in Maleae; Wikipedia Cannabaceae: ovary usually superior.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Rosales page (read 2026-10-16): one ovule per carpel; Rosaceae one to many carpels. Urticalean families 1-2 carpels (Wikipedia Cannabaceae: two joined), Rhamnaceae 2-3. Typical 2 is my weighting.
